simple.meaning: גָּלַשׁ (gâlash) is a Hebrew action word meaning “probably to caper (as a goat).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Song of Solomon, beginning at Song of Songs 4:1. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גָּלַשׁ (H1570) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גָּלַשׁ (gâlash) / H1570 is traced through Song of Songs 4:1, Song of Songs 6:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1570. galash [ גָּלַשׁ ] verb sit, sit up , possibly also recline (compare Arabic sit up ; so Thes De and others (not Ew)) — only Qal Perfect (שֶׁ)גָָּֽלִשׁוּ Song 4:1 ; 6:5 גִּלְעָד מ(הר) שֶׁגָּלְשׁוּ of flocks of goats, in simile of a woman's hair; construction & sense rather awkward. גַּם see below גמם .
